Vendetta explains on Thessia that the patterns concerning the development of galactic civilization and the cycles of extinction are too regular and repetitive to be coincidence. According to the VI, the galaxy experiences the same paths and conflicts during each cycle \- "the same peaks of evolution, the same valleys of dissolution" \- expressed in different forms. It infers that the Reapers are servants of this pattern, not the creators of it. The Reapers' true master and motive, however, remained largely unknown until Commander Shepard's meeting with the Catalyst itself. The Reapers leave no evidence of their conquest, nor of their existence – only desolate, barren ruins of those who came before. Extant information on them is so scant that they are known merely as "boogeymen" at best in many cultures' ancient legends. The trap created by the Reapers was simple. A sentient species would develop an FTL drive, but would still be limited in its speed. By leaving a network of relays capable of instant transport across the galaxy that led to the impressive Citadel, the Reapers ensured that it would become the center of galactic civilization. Further, Sovereign implies that the presence of the mass relays would lead the sentient species down a predetermined route with regards to weapons and armor technology (both of which are based upon element zero technology for the Citadel races). As Sovereign explains, "By using it \[mass relay technology] your society develops along the paths we desire." The relays also serve to reduce the amount of time it takes for galactic civilization to advance, thus shortening the time between the Reapers' harvests. Once the sentient races have established themselves on the Citadel with the aid of the keepers, a lone Reaper vanguard stationed within the galaxy sends a signal to the Citadel, instructing the keepers to activate the station’s hidden mass relay. This opens a path between the Citadel and dark space. The Reapers then flood through, killing the leaders of the assembled species before branching out and harvesting all spacefaring life around them. Because the Reapers first enter the galaxy at the point that they have ensured will be the center of galactic politics, information and finance, they are able to cripple any resistance almost before the Citadel civilizations have any idea that they are under attack. The Citadel also gives them control of the relay network, cutting off star systems from each other and destroying communications. The Reapers then use their control of the Citadel and its data to begin the most sinister phase of their attack. Records allow them to track down every settled planet and attack them, harvesting their populations or enslaving them through indoctrination. Once they have harvested the galaxy, the Reapers wipe every trace of their existence from record and retreat back into dark space.

Keepers continue to perform their normal routines during most of the Reaper invasion in 2186\. Tunnels normally used by keepers are used as escape routes by Cerberus forces when they launched an abortive attack against the Citadel. Near the end of the war, the Citadel is captured by Reaper forces and moved over Earth. The Reapers use parts of the Citadel as a dumping ground for human corpses, and the keepers assist in processing the bodies.

evidence.page: Chorban's Keeper Scans and His Falling-Out With Jahleed
evidence.text: Chorban's Keeper Scans and His Falling-Out With Jahleed. 2183, Citadel, during the hunt for Saren the Citadel Tower, the C-Sec offices, then the Lower Markets of the Wards If Chorban survived and Shepard scanned all or most of the keepers, he emails Shepard in 2185 with his findings: the keepers are bio-engineered, and comparison with material from Saren's flagship Sovereign shows they were engineered millions of years ago by the same makers, meaning the Citadel likely was not built by the Protheans. His genetic readings suggest the keepers are set to react to a signal roughly every 50,000 years, the last such interval coinciding with the Protheans' disappearance and due again around now, meaning old technology might have "nasty surprises" waiting. He notes no one else on the Citadel will listen to him.

The Reapers were a highly advanced machine race of synthetic-organic starships that hibernated in dark space, the mostly starless void between galaxies, dormant for fifty thousand years at a time before returning to harvest the galaxy's advanced life. Their true name was unknown; "Reapers" was a label bestowed by the Protheans, and the geth called them the Old Machines. Each Reaper was described as "billions of organic minds, uploaded and conjoined within immortal machine bodies," its core built in the image of the species harvested to create it while its exterior followed a standardized design derived from the Leviathans, an ancient aquatic race. Reapers ranged from 160 meters to over two kilometers in length. Subtypes included Harbinger (the first Reaper, largest in the armada), Sovereign-class Capital Ships (two kilometers long, with a spinal magnetohydrodynamic cannon yielding 132 to 450 kilotons), Troop Transports and Processors (non-sentient, remotely controlled), and 160-meter Destroyers that could unfold their legs to walk as heavy ground units.

The Reapers built the Citadel and mass relay network as a trap, ensuring galactic civilization would develop along predictable technological paths centered on the Citadel and could be crippled at a stroke. A vanguard within the galaxy would signal the Citadel, the keepers would open its hidden relay, and the Reaper fleet would flood in, kill the leaders of the assembled species, then use Citadel records to hunt every settled world. Victims were rounded into camps by husks, sorted by genetic fitness, loaded into Processor pods, and dissolved by nanides into genetic paste used to build new Reapers, their minds preserved as the new Reaper's gestalt consciousness. Those deemed unsuitable were converted into husks via dragon's teeth. Reaper technology also relied on indoctrination, a permanent mental erosion that turned nearby organics into willing slaves.

The Reapers were created by the Leviathans' "Intelligence," built to solve the cycle of organics and synthetics destroying each other; it instead processed the Leviathans into Harbinger and began cyclical purges spanning millions of years. Fifty thousand years before the modern era they wiped out the Protheans, though a cadre on Ilos survived in stasis and altered the Citadel signal, delaying the next invasion. Sovereign, acting as vanguard, was found in the Perseus Veil, swayed geth heretics, and used Saren Arterius to locate the Conduit; it assaulted the Citadel in 2183 and was destroyed by the Alliance Fleet. The Collectors, repurposed Protheans, later abducted humans to build a Human-Reaper, which Shepard destroyed in 2185. Shepard delayed the invasion again by destroying the Alpha Relay in the Bahak System, killing 300,000 batarians. The Reapers returned in 2186, destroyed the Batarian Hegemony within days, and overran Earth, Palaven, Thessia and more. Shepard unified the galaxy, cured the genophage, freed the geth at Rannoch, and recruited the Leviathans. The Crucible superweapon, requiring the Citadel as its Catalyst, offered Shepard the choice of Destroy, Control, or Synthesis, with a refusal option that let the cycle continue.

The Citadel was a colossal deep-space station in the Widow system of the Serpent Nebula, serving as the capital of the Citadel Council and the political and cultural heart of Citadel space. Roughly pentagram-shaped, it consisted of a central ring about 7.2 km in diameter from which five arms, the Wards, extended, each about 43.6 km long; open, the station measured 44.7 km in length, housed about 13.2 million people plus the keepers, and could close its arms into an armored cylinder about 45 km long in emergencies. Gravity was simulated through rotation. The asari discovered the station in 580 BCE, soon joined by the salarians and then the volus; other races gained embassies as they were contacted, and the Council eventually comprised asari, salarians, and turians. The station's builders, its core and master control unit, its construction material, and the nature of its keeper caretakers all remained mysteries. It was long believed to have been built by the Protheans, but they were merely the last race to use it before the asari arrived. In truth, the Citadel and the mass relays were creations of the Reapers, built to facilitate their cycle of galactic genocide: the station was an inactive mass relay leading to dark space, and the keepers were placed to keep its occupants from discovering its key functions, allowing the Reapers to wipe out galactic leadership in a single strike. According to the VI Vigil, the last Protheans used the Conduit to reach the Citadel and disrupt the cycle, forcing the Reapers to travel to the Milky Way at normal FTL speeds, though those Protheans likely starved to death on the station. The Presidium ring held government offices, embassies, shops, and an artificial 20-hour day-night cycle, monitored by the VI Avina; the Citadel Tower housed the Council Chambers and station traffic control. The Wards were the densely populated residential and commercial arms, policed by roughly 200,000 C-Sec officers and home to the club Flux, the Silversun Strip, and the Citadel Archives; Barla Von called them the cultural heart of Citadel space. Defenses included the hard-to-navigate Serpent Nebula, the Citadel Fleet led by the asari dreadnought Destiny Ascension, rapid mass relay reinforcement, the closing hull, and anti-fighter turrets. Unique inhabitants included the duct rats, homeless children living in the ventilation system, among them Mouse, an informant for Thane Krios, and the bio-engineered insectoid keepers. In 2186 the Illusive Man fled to the Citadel and alerted the Reapers, who seized it and moved it into Earth's orbit; the Catalyst needed to complete the Crucible was revealed to be part of the station. During the battle for Earth, Commander Shepard boarded via a transport beam, opened the Wards for the Crucible to attach, and met the Catalyst, the Intelligence controlling the Reapers, then chose to destroy the Reapers, control them, or merge organic and synthetic life; the Citadel amplified the Crucible's energy and transmitted it to the Charon Relay and the wider relay network. Depending on the choice, the Citadel and relays were severely damaged and later rebuilt, or the Citadel remained intact while the relays were damaged. Proposed development names for the station included "Optigon" and "Oculon," and "C-Sec" was at one point "Oc-Sec."

evidence.page: The Admiralty Board's Ask, and Tali's Return
evidence.text: The Admiralty Board's Ask, and Tali's Return. 2186, Priority: Perseus Veil, after the failed Cerberus coup on the Citadel the Normandy's war room, docked with the Quarian Envoy Ship at Dholen in the Far Rim In the Normandy's war room the Migrant Fleet's admirals explained that they had opened an all-out war on the geth, pushing them back toward Rannoch, after the Reapers upgraded the geth — and that their fleet was now trapped. They asked the Normandy to disable a geth dreadnought broadcasting the Reaper signal.

Henry Lawson's Standoff at Sanctuary. 2186, during Priority: Horizon, as the Reapers overrun Sanctuary the upper laboratories of the Sanctuary facility, Horizon Shepard's squad reached Sanctuary tracking Kai Leng after Thessia. The facility, advertised galaxy-wide as a refugee haven, was a Cerberus operation run by Henry Lawson: refugees were processed into husks and test subjects while Henry researched copying the Reaper signal that controlled them. Henry had located Oriana and brought her there; the Reapers, detecting his work, were assaulting the facility as Shepard arrived.

Mass Effect: Deception is the fourth Mass Effect tie-in novel, released January 31, 2012. Unlike the previous three novels, which were written by Drew Karpyshyn, Deception was written by William C. Dietz.

The story follows Navy admiral David Anderson and his partner Kahlee Sanders as they search for a way to stop the cycle of the Reapers, sentient machines that invade the galaxy every fifty thousand years to harvest all organic life. They uncover evidence that the Reaper threat is real, and in doing so expose the machinations of Cerberus and its leader, the Illusive Man, putting them in mortal danger. They find an unlikely ally in Gillian Grayson, a young woman with extraordinary biotic powers who was once the subject of horrifying experiments and is now free and mastering her abilities. After learning that Cerberus caused her father's death, Gillian swears vengeance against the group and the Illusive Man, threatening to unravel Anderson and Kahlee's efforts.

The novel drew fan criticism for numerous continuity and factual errors. BioWare and Del Rey Books apologized and announced that changes would be made to future editions; on December 14, 2012, BioWare said they were checking with the publisher about updates, but no revised edition has been released. Full plot details are covered on the separate Storyline page.

The Reapers have existed for at least a billion years, based upon findings on the Leviathan of Dis, an ancient Reaper corpse. Before the Reapers came to be, the galaxy was under the thrall of a race known as Leviathans. They created an "Intelligence" to solve the problem of organics and synthetics killing each other. However, this Intelligence turned on them, slaughtering most of their kind and processing others into the very first true Reaper, Harbinger. Harbinger's form, that of the Leviathans themselves, became the template for subsequent Reapers harvested from the galaxy's races on cyclical purges over the next millions of years. In order to speed up the time between harvests, the Reapers constructed the mass relay network and the Citadel to coordinate it. Engineered creatures called keepers were placed on the Citadel to maintain the station during their absence and to open it for them when they decide to invade. Fifty thousand years before the current galactic era, the Reapers initiated a purge against the Protheans, the dominant spacefaring lifeforms at the time. The Protheans tried to resist like so many others before them, only to fail due to the Reapers' physical and insidious might.

evidence.text: More than 50,000 years ago, before the dawn of their civilization, the early Turians were known to elder spacefaring species such as the Protheans, but were considered too primitive to be of any concern to the Prothean empire. Commander Shepard first hears of the Thorian from Lizbeth Baynham, who tentatively suggests that it might be why the geth are attacking the colonists on Feros. Shepard can learn more from the ExoGeni VI; once freed from the Thorian, Shiala then tells Shepard its history. According to Shiala, the Thorian existed on Feros long before the Protheans arrived. It would spend thousands of years in hibernation, then awake for "a few frantic centuries" of activity before resting again. When the Protheans arrived and began building the metropolis that would eventually cover Feros, the curious Thorian studied them, likely made several of them into its thralls, and even absorbed them after they died, allowing them to become a part of its expanding consciousness. From the Protheans, the Thorian's mind gradually absorbed the knowledge that would form the Cipher. The Thorian survived the cataclysm that destroyed the Protheans, and continued to grow across Feros for the next fifty thousand years.

The Thorian, also called Species 37, was an ancient sentient plant at least fifty thousand years old, its true age unknowable because it could hibernate for millennia. It was a unique creature with telepathic and mind-controlling abilities and a massive sensory network, releasing airborne spores that let it control anyone who inhaled them, using pain to enforce obedience. These "thralls" tended the Thorian and obeyed its will. According to the ExoGeni Corporation VI, it was essentially "a weave of tendrils" covering much of the surface of Feros, with some sensory tendrils kilometres long, gathered in places into neural nodes. It regarded other sentients only as potential thralls and called itself "The Old Growth."

The Thorian existed on Feros before the Protheans arrived. It studied the Protheans as they built their metropolis, made some into thralls and absorbed them after death, and its mind gradually acquired the knowledge that formed the Cipher. It survived the cataclysm that destroyed the Protheans and kept growing for fifty thousand years. In the late 2170s ExoGeni settled a colony, Zhu's Hope, in a ruined skyscraper above its lair. In 2183 a survey team stumbled into the lair and was infected; ExoGeni isolated the colony to study the Thorian instead of protecting the colonists, and within a month 85% of Zhu's Hope was enthralled. Some, like Ian Newstead, resisted for a time.

Saren Arterius learned of the Thorian's link to the Protheans and traded the asari commando Shiala to it as a sacrifice; Shiala melded with it, gained the Cipher, and transferred it to Saren, who then ordered his geth to destroy the Thorian and all evidence of it. The enthralled colonists blocked the lair with the wrecked freighter Borealis and fought to the death. Commander Shepard arrived to investigate; the Thorian initially had the colonists and the merchant Ledra help Shepard fight the geth, then turned them hostile once Shepard learned the truth at the ExoGeni building. Fai Dan broke the Thorian's control and shot himself rather than attack Shepard. In the lair the Thorian produced a clone of Shiala to speak for it, dismissed humans as "meat, good only to dig or decompose," and sent clones and Thorian Creepers at the squad. Shepard destroyed the neural nodes, dislodging the Thorian and sending it plunging to its death. Shiala, if spared, mourned it as a unique life form.

Afterward ExoGeni removed the remains, but lingering spore effects gave former victims headaches and shared pain sensations; Shiala's skin turned green and her biotics became unstable. In 2186 the residual hive-mind effects helped the colonists coordinate against the Reapers long enough to evacuate. In the Leviathan investigation, Dr. Garret Bryson cited the Thorian as a species that developed using only organic tools, without mass relays or Reaper technology, and compared Leviathan's long survival to it.
